The problem? The New 3DS XL is $199.99 and the regular New 3DS retails for $149.99 with a game I already own.

Then came Black Friday's Super Mario Black Edition New 3DS for $99. It was a sweet enough deal that I waited in line for 2 hours on Thanksgiving Day to hit Target and get my hands on one, complete with 5% off Target Red Card bonus. The price was perfect and the smaller size might mean better portability and fewer drops.

This past Saturday morning, like a kid at Christmas, I did my System Transfer from the o3DSXL to the n3DS, and spent portions of the day getting accustomed to my n3DS, including getting a few SNES Virtual Console titles.

Well... despite threads here saying the screen size difference isn't that bad. It's bad for Virtual Console titles. 3DS games are fine, but the Virtual Console NES and SNES games are microscopic on the regular n3DS. Unbearably microscopic.

I missed my o3DSXL immediately.

So today, Target has everything 15% off, and with a Red card, you get another 5% off. So I managed to pick up a Black n3DSXL today... but alas, I have to wait until the 7-day System Transfer lockout expires this coming Saturday, so I can transfer over to my n3DSXL, format the Super Mario Black n3DS, and then return it to Target for my money back.

So, the point of this narrative is to tell o3DSXL system users that if you currently have an o3DSXL and want to get a n3DS system, if you find yourself playing lots of Virtual Console titles and don't see yourself doing much with faceplates, you better get the n3DSXL.
